sentences.text: Hello, and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today, we will talk about Uruguay.
Uruguay is a small, peaceful,
and beautiful country in South America.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Uruguay?
Uruguay is in South America.
It is next to Brazil and Argentina.
To the south, it touches the Atlantic Ocean.
It has beaches, rivers, and green hills.
What is the capital city of Uruguay?
The capital city is Montevideo.
Montevideo is by the sea.
It has parks, markets,
old buildings, and modern areas.
It is the largest city in Uruguay.
Other towns include Punta del Este,
a beach city for tourists.
Salto, known for hot springs.
Colonia del Sacramento,
a UNESCO World Heritage City with old streets.
How many people live in Uruguay?
About 3.5 million people live in Uruguay.
It is one of the smallest countries in South America by population.
Most people live near the coast or in Montevideo.
What language do people speak in Uruguay?
The official language is Spanish.
People speak it with a real platent accent like in Argentina.
Many people also speak some Portuguese near Brazil
and a little English in tourist areas.
What is the weather like in Uruguay?
Uruguay has a mild climate.
Warm summers from December to March.
Cool winters from June to August.
It rains all year, but not too much.
The weather is good for farming and outdoor life.
What does Uruguay look like?
Uruguay has long beaches,
flat land, and rolling hills.
Farms and ranches, called Estancias,
rivers like the Rio de la Plata and Rio Uruguay.
It is a green and calm country.
What animals live in Uruguay?
In Uruguay, you can see cows,
horses, and sheep on farms.
Foxes, armadillos, and birds in nature.
Seals, sea lions, and whales along the coast.
Two cans and parrots and some forests.
Uruguay has many cattle and beef is very important.
What do people eat in Uruguay?
Uruguay and food is simple, meaty, and delicious.
People eat beef, chicken, and sausages.
Bread, pasta, and rice.
Potatoes, lettuce, and tomatoes.
Popular dishes, asado, grilled meat, often cooked outside.
Chivito, a big sandwich with steak, egg, and vegetables.
Empanadas, pastries filled with meat or cheese.
Tortas fritas, fried dough, often eaten when it rains.
What do people drink in Uruguay?
People drink water, juice, and coffee.
Mate, a strong tea made from your beliefs,
shared with friends, milk and soft drinks.
Adults may drink wine or beer.
Mate is very popular and part of daily life.
What is life like in Uruguay?
Life in Uruguay is relaxed, safe, and social.
People enjoy drinking mate with friends,
going to the beach, watching football,
listening to music and dancing,
spending time with family.
Many people live in quiet towns and enjoy a simple life.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Carnival in February with music and parades.
Independence Day, August 25th.
Christmas and New Year Easter Week,
called Tourism Week, football games.
Very important to many people.
People dance kendombe, a drum-based music and dance
from African traditions.
Some fun facts about Uruguay.
Uruguay was the first country in the world
to give free laptops to all school children.
Football, soccer, is the national passion
Uruguay won the first World Cup in 1930.
The flag is white and blue with a yellow sun.
It is one of the most peaceful and democratic
countries in South America.
Now you know many things about Uruguay.
You know where it is, what people eat,
and how they live.
You learned about the beaches, football, and mate.
Well done.
I am Emily.
Goodbye, or as they say in Spanish, Adios!
